name: Solenne Atelier Velvet Gala Half-Glove
description:
Opera-length evening gloves cut from triple-pile synthetic velvet in deep oxblood or midnight lacquer, worn to the upper arm with a structured boning channel at the elbow that keeps the drape architectural. The back of the hand is open from knuckle to wrist — a deliberate cutaway that exposes chrome knuckle plating, bioluminescent skin, or decorative subdermal implants as a designed feature rather than an afterthought.

The cuff edge is finished with a single strand of heat-reactive thread that shifts between gold and copper tones under body warmth. Interior is raw silk-analog for ease over chrome or scaled geneware arms. Clasp at the inner wrist is a magnetic Solenne-logo closure, recessed and invisible when fastened.
functionality: Knuckle-to-wrist cutaway frames chrome or geneware as intentional display. Heat-reactive thread activates under body warmth for dynamic color shift. Silk-analog lining slides smoothly over chrome or scaled arms. Magnetic clasp allows single-handed fastening.
what_it_says: Your augmentations and modifications aren't concealed — they're the centerpiece, and you had them dressed by someone who charges more than most people earn in a year.
story_hooks: A pair of Solenne gala gloves is found in a Circuit pawn shop — the magnetic clasp contains a micro-storage chip with encrypted Spire-level financial data.
A Tier 5 socialite's gloves fail to close at a Spire event, revealing chrome knuckles bearing a the Gray Zone-gang tattoo laser-etched into the metal — a past they paid to forget.

physical_description.visual_profile: Opera-length statement glove extending to upper arm with dramatic architectural silhouette. The signature cutaway across the back of the hand creates a bold asymmetrical negative space—a deliberate design choice that transforms augmented limbs into display pieces rather than covering them. The garment reads as haute couture meets cybernetic pragmatism: luxe and confrontational.
physical_description.fit: Precise, structured compression fit through the forearm with rigid boning channels at the elbow that maintain dramatic vertical drape. Hand opening is cut generously to accommodate varying cybernetic widths without binding. Interior contours to the arm with subtle ergonomic support.
physical_description.primary_material: Triple-pile synthetic velvet (oxblood or midnight lacquer colorway). Interior lined with raw silk-analog for smooth slip over chrome, hydraulic, or scaled geneware arms.
physical_description.texture: Exterior pile is lush and light-absorbing—surface reads as almost liquid in dim light, with subtle sheen variation following the nap direction. Heat-reactive gold-to-copper thread edge creates fine tactile line at cuff. Interior is smooth, cool, frictionless.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep oxblood red or midnight lacquer (near-black with blue undertone). Heat-reactive cuff thread shifts from warm gold to oxidized copper as body heat activates it. Interior raw silk-analog in neutral ivory or grey.
physical_description.closures: Recessed magnetic closure at inner wrist bearing Solenne logo—invisible when fastened, designed to keep exterior surface pristine and uninterrupted.
distinctive_features: Open cutaway across back of hand (knuckle to wrist) deliberately exposing chrome plating, bioluminescent subdermal work, or decorative implants
Structured boning channels at elbow maintaining architectural vertical fold
Heat-reactive thread at cuff edge transitioning gold→copper under body warmth
Raw silk-analog interior for compatibility with cybernetic limbs
Recessed magnetic Solenne Atelier logo closure
Triple-pile velvet construction for light-absorbing depth
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 1 luxury. Despite being produced by a Tier 5 corpo, these gloves are priced and positioned as high-end evening wear. The deliberate embrace of visible augmentation signals post-corpo wealth—someone secure enough to display rather than hide.
physical_description.cultural_context: Gala-circuit, corpo social climbers, cybermodding enthusiasts who treat augmentation as fashion statement. Wearer is signaling: I have chrome, I'm proud of it, and I can afford velvet that costs more than most monthly wages. Popular among medical-tech executives, genetic modders, and the nouveau-riche augmentation elite.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine to lightly worn. These are investment pieces maintained with obsessive care. Any visible wear would be cosmetic creasing from storage or careful use—velvet pile self-recovers. Magnetic clasp remains perfectly recessed. Heat-reactive thread maintains color shift with no fading.
